facts.fact: We Are Tech Africa reports that the government presented DIGI-CoR, a CFA 92 billion (US$163 million) programme over three years, to technical and financial partners in Yaoundé on 2 June 2026; it is to deploy digital infrastructure, improve connectivity, equip decentralised local authorities with IT and energy systems and set up interoperable platforms.

We Are Tech Africa states that DIGI-CoR is the government's own programme for the decentralised local authorities, presented by it to partners on 2 June 2026, with local authorities to rely on shared resources for hosting, cybersecurity and service management.

We Are Tech Africa states that on 2 June 2026 Cameroon was still seeking financing for DIGI-CoR's CFA 92 billion from technical and financial partners; no domestic budget line and no committed funder is named.

On 2 June 2026 the government presented DIGI-CoR, a CFA 92 billion programme that includes improving the connectivity of decentralised local authorities, to funders in Yaoundé; the programme was unfunded and nothing was reported as deployed.

systems.tiers: decentralised local authorities, municipalities and regions; programme at the financing stage in June 2026, covering infrastructure, connectivity, IT and energy equipment, shared hosting and interoperable platforms

systems.system: structured computer networks of local authorities
systems.tiers: 68.5% of decentralised local authorities lack one and 57.8% employ no staff trained in digital tools, per government data presented 2 June 2026

systems.owner: FEICOM, the Special Fund for Equipment and Inter-Municipal Intervention

note: DIGI-CoR is recorded as a connection programme because the article says it will improve connectivity; the 68.5% figure is of office computer networks and the 145 of equipment, neither stated as a connection, so neither gives a fact on local governments connected.
